svg.title: One Evidence Desk, Three Distinct Recovery Lanes
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-three-lane-recovery-workflow; chart type: process_flow; title: One Evidence Desk, Three Distinct Recovery Lanes; subtitle: Classify first; verify eligibility before assigning collectible value.; chapter number: 1; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Drawback, tariff refunds, and antitrust distributions are alternative routes through this workflow, not sequential recoveries on the same dollars. Importer duty principal, merchant purchase volume, and gross settlement pools never become operator revenue. Formal customs filings use a licensed 19 CFR Part 111 customs broker or trade counsel with valid Customs Powers of Attorney.; caption: The operator sells evidence assembly and recovery coordination; only earned contingency fees enter the revenue scorecard.; stages: label: Authorize the account; value: Written scope and record access; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Execute the recovery agreement, identify the claimant entity, document record-access authority, and price a zero-upfront 25%–35% contingency on realized recoveries. Obtain the required Customs Power of Attorney directly for the filing professional.; label: Route the recovery; value: Three separate eligibility ledgers; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Create distinct ledgers for 19 U.S.C. § 1313 drawback, 19 U.S.C. § 1514 protests or ACE Post-Summary Correction, and existing B2B antitrust settlements. Assign each ledger its own deadline, collectible base, cost budget, and cash estimate.; label: Reconcile primary evidence; value: Entry, export, or purchase proof; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Use ImportGenius or Panjiva for discovery, then reconcile authorized ACE CBP Form 7501 records, duty payments, export bills of lading, and inventory movements. For settlements, reconcile accounts-payable or processor records to class periods. Manifest matches and eight-digit HTS matches are candidate links, not proof of statutory eligibility.; label: Submit the correct packet; value: Professional filing or permitted submission; numeric value: 4.0; detail: The broker or trade counsel files the correct customs route and retains Part 190 evidence for drawback. Settlement packets follow the court-approved claim form, allocation plan, third-party filer rules, and claimant authorization. Block duplicate claims and unsupported substitutions before submission.; label: Reconcile cash and fee; value: Realized recovery to earned revenue; numeric value: 5.0; detail: Match the agency refund or administrator distribution to the claimant ledger, resolve offsets and reversals, and calculate the contracted earned fee. Record client recovery principal separately from operator consideration; retain an auditable bridge from payment notice to fee invoice.

rect.title: label: Route the recovery; value: Three separate eligibility ledgers; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Create distinct ledgers for 19 U.S.C. § 1313 drawback, 19 U.S.C. § 1514 protests or ACE Post-Summary Correction, and existing B2B antitrust settlements. Assign each ledger its own deadline, collectible base, cost budget, and cash estimate.

text.title: Create distinct ledgers for 19 U.S.C. § 1313 drawback, 19 U.S.C. § 1514 protests or ACE Post-Summary Correction, and existing B2B antitrust settlements. Assign each ledger its own deadline, collectible base, cost budget, and cash estimate.

rect.title: label: Reconcile primary evidence; value: Entry, export, or purchase proof; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Use ImportGenius or Panjiva for discovery, then reconcile authorized ACE CBP Form 7501 records, duty payments, export bills of lading, and inventory movements. For settlements, reconcile accounts-payable or processor records to class periods. Manifest matches and eight-digit HTS matches are candidate links, not proof of statutory eligibility.

text.title: Assumptions: Drawback, tariff refunds, and antitrust distributions are alternative routes through this workflow, not sequential recoveries on the same dollars. Importer duty principal, merchant purchase volume, and gross settlement pools never become operator revenue. Formal customs filings use a licensed 19 CFR Part 111 customs broker or trade counsel with valid Customs Powers of Attorney.
